question: A junior developer is trying to make a reusable object so that a record status will show up as an icon with a specific color. If no status is designated, then "N/A" should display. They have already created relevant constants for all status values and colors needed. This status will be used both on the record list and within the record summary view. Which strategy should you recommend? A. Create an interface that includes an a!match(), which is used to select a a!iconIndicator() or defaulted a!richTextItem("N/A") based on a rule input made for the value parameter of the a!match(). B. Create an expression that includes a a!richTextDisplayField(), where a!match() is used to select a a!richTextIcon() or defaulted a!richTextItem("N/A") based on a rule input made for the value parameter of the a!match(). C. Create expressions for each a!richTextIcon() option with appropriate constants. Use an a!match() in the target interface to choose from the icon expressions or a!richTextItem("N/A"), based on the target data's status.

You are evaluating a junior developer's work. The junior developer was tasked with exposing a record type's data to a third-party service outside of Appian. In the Appian environment, they created a web API object, a system administrator service account, and an API key for the service account from the Appian Administration Console. You have verified through Postman that the web API operates as expected. What should you recommend to the junior developer to ensure their implementation meets all security best practices? A. Convert the web API to an HTTPS endpoint and add the resulting Client Certificate to the target environment's Administration Console. B. Deactivate the API key, and use OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials to authenticate and audit all calls made from the environment. C. Convert the service account to a Basic user, and ensure the service account has Viewer permissions to the source record type and the web API.
